premise: forced eviction; hidden-swap-ms, not wall clock; Fresh-277 cannot exhibit contention

mechanism.headline: 100% of the prediction budget lies in calls whose latency falls between 1x and 2x the KV cost. Calls beyond 2x contribute EXACTLY ZERO.
mechanism.why: For L >= 2*kv the deadline fires at kv with remaining L-kv >= kv, so it already hides the full swap with zero exposure and the oracle cannot improve on it. For L just above the threshold the deadline fires with almost no remaining time and is exposed by nearly the whole kv, while the oracle fires at L-kv and hides all of it. The budget is the exposure the deadline eats on calls that only just outlive it.
mechanism.target_population: 309 of 13410 rows at kv=3500 and 325 of 13410 at kv=5000, i.e. 2.3-2.4% of calls. Capturing the budget requires deciding at t~0 that a call will land in that narrow band, not merely that it will be long.
mechanism.reframes_the_whole_lane: Every predictor built in this repo targets P(long), i.e. P(L > kv). That is the WRONG target: among long calls, those beyond 2x kv carry no budget at all. The correct target is P(kv < L < 2*kv), a narrow-band discrimination on ~2.4% of calls. This explains why four committed NO-GOs all failed while the budget was large the whole time.

verdict: Budget is 88.9% of deadline utility at kv=3500 and 84.8% at kv=5000, both CIs excluding zero, so under the frozen bands prediction is worth continued investment. But the shipped robust_clock captures 1.4% and 8.0% of it. The barrier is not that prediction is impossible; it is that every predictor here optimised the wrong target.
